200.description:
One Alberta Gazette issue as published text (verbatim, from the King's Printer text version), located by year, part ('1', '2' or 'registrar' for the Registrar's Periodical) and issue ordinal. post.description: After search_legislation. Use the ISBN of a '(Download Version)' record. Pass `section` (e.g. '25' or '23.1') for a single section; without it every section of the title is returned (acts can run to hundreds of sections).

isbn.description: Catalogue ISBN from search_legislation (e.g. 9780779858644 for the Employment Standards Code download version). Pattern: ^[0-9]{10}([0-9]{3})?$.

section.description: Section number as printed ('25', '23.1'); 's. 25' and 'section 25' are accepted. Unknown section: not_found.

provider.summary: Official provider example; checked against AIsa request constraints

200.description:
One consolidated act or regulation by catalogue ISBN: catalogue metadata (citation, status, responsible ministry, 'Current to' date, pages), the consolidation date printed on the text ('Current as of'), for regulations the '(Consolidated up to AR)' marker and enabling act, the associated regulations, the PDF URL and the full text split into sections with number, marginal heading, part/division, paragraphs and the per-section amendment history line (e.g. 'RSA 2000 cE-9 s25;2017 c9 s12'). `section` returns one section only.

The response contains the tool result directly.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `associated_regulations` | object[] | Acts: the regulations listed under 'Following are the associated Regulations'. Empty for regulations and for acts without any. |
| `citation` | string | Chapter/Regulation as printed in the catalogue. |
| `consolidated_up_to` | string | Regulations: the '(Consolidated up to NNN/YYYY)' marker, i.e. the last amending regulation applied. Null for acts. |
| `current_as_of` | string | ISO date from 'Current as of Month DD, YYYY' on the text page: the office consolidation date of the text returned. Null only when no online text exists. |
| `current_to` | string | ISO date from the catalogue's 'Current to MM/DD/YYYY'; null when not printed. |
| `description` | string | Catalogue blurb. |
| `enabling_act` | string | Regulations: the enabling act named above the title. Null for acts. |
| `format` | string |  |
| `html_url` | string | 1266.cfm HTML text viewer; null when the record is a paid-only format without online text. |
| `isbn` | string |  |
| `kind` | string |  |
| `ministry` | object | Responsible ministry (catalogue code and name); null when the catalogue prints none (regulations usually inherit it from the act). |
| `observed_at_ms` | number |  |
| `pages` | number |  |
| `pdf_url` | string | 1266.cfm PDF viewer link. |
| `related_act_isbn` | string | Regulations: ISBN of the enabling act's catalogue record ('Related Act' link). Null for acts. |
| `section_count` | number | Sections found in the whole text (before any `section` filter). |
| `sections` | object[] |  |
| `source_url` | string | Catalogue detail page (570.cfm?frm_isbn=...). |
| `status` | string | Catalogue status, normally 'Office Consolidation'. |
| `title` | string |  |


These are the provider's documented fields. Field requiredness, nullability and nested object structures are specified only where the descriptions explicitly say so.

associated_regulations.title: Employment Standards Regulation (Comes with paper insert including changes from AR 136/2025 - eff Sep 1, 2025 & AR 281/2025 - eff Jan 1, 2026)

value.description: The Employment Standards Code establishes Alberta’s minimum standards of employment in many areas including payment of wages, hours of work, overtime, vacation and holidays, leaves and termination of employment. It establishes the processes by which an employee can seek recourse if the standards have not been met.

sections.division: Division 5 General Holidays and General Holiday Pay
sections.heading: General holidays in Alberta
sections.text:
The following days are general holidays in Alberta:
(a) New Year’s Day,
(b) Alberta Family Day,
(c) Good Friday,
(d) Victoria Day,
(e) Canada Day,
(f) Labour Day,
(g) Thanksgiving Day,
(h) Remembrance Day,
(i) Christmas Day,
(j) any other day designated, by regulation, as a general holiday by the Lieutenant Governor in Council, and
(k) any other day designated as a general holiday under an agreement between an employer and employees, or otherwise designated as a general holiday by an employer.

value.title: Employment Standards Code

post.description: Start here to find the ISBN of an act or regulation. Pass `query` for title words (POST keyword search; the site matches title words, not full text) or `citation` for an exact chapter/regulation number such as '14/1997' (regulation) or 'E-9 RSA 2000' (act).

citation.description: Exact chapter/regulation citation as printed in the catalogue: regulations 'NNN/YYYY' (e.g. '14/1997'), acts 'E-9 RSA 2000' or 'A-37.7 2026'. 'RSA 2000 cE-9' and 'SA 2026 cA-37.7' forms are normalised. Mutually exclusive with `query`.

query.description: Title keywords, e.g. 'employment standards'. Mutually exclusive with `citation`.

200.description:
Search the Laws Online catalogue of current consolidated Alberta acts and regulations by title keyword or by exact chapter/regulation citation. Returns catalogue records (title, ISBN, citation, product format). Only '(Download Version)' records carry free HTML/PDF text; use their ISBN with get_legislation.

The response contains the tool result directly.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `count` | number | The 'N records found' count printed by the catalogue; 0 for 'No records found'. |
| `observed_at_ms` | number |  |
| `records` | object[] |  |
| `search_by` | string |  |
| `source_url` | string | The catalogue page that answered (the form is POSTed to it). |
| `term` | string | The term as sent to the catalogue (after citation normalisation). |


These are the provider's documented fields. Field requiredness, nullability and nested object structures are specified only where the descriptions explicitly say so.
